name: Moving data across spaces and distributions
gist: Sometimes data lives in different spaces (high-dimensional to low-dimensional, one distribution to another). How do you transport or transform it efficiently while preserving structure?
explain: Imagine you train a model to recognize images from high-quality cameras, but then you need it to work on low-resolution phone photos. Or you train on photos of dogs in good lighting, but it needs to work on dark, blurry photos from security cameras. The data has shifted—it has moved to a different space. The model learned from high-quality photos, and the skills it learned do not transfer perfectly to blurry photos. Alternatively, you have raw data that lives in a complicated high-dimensional space (an image is millions of pixel values), but you want to learn relationships in a simpler lower-dimensional space where similar images are close together.

The research problem is that transforming or transporting data between these spaces while keeping structure intact is tricky. If you blindly compress a dataset from high to low dimensions, you might line up dissimilar examples near each other and miss clusters. If you adapt a model to handle lower-quality images, you need to know which features of the training data are important (the edges of objects) and which are accidents of the camera (the exact lighting). You also need to do this without labels: you usually do not have experts labeling every example from the new dataset.

Papers use several strategies. Some learn transformations that map between distributions while keeping distances between examples roughly the same—if two high-quality photos were similar, their low-quality versions should still be similar. Others use adversarial methods: train two networks in competition, where one network adapts the source data toward the target distribution and another network tries to detect whether examples come from source or target. If the adaptation is good enough to fool the detector, the transformation worked. Some papers use optimal transport, which borrows math from economics about moving goods with minimum shipping cost—applied here, it finds the cheapest way to move a probability distribution from one space to another. The connection is that these methods all preserve local structure: nearby points stay nearby after transformation.

papers.title: A Memory-Efficient Hierarchical Algorithm for Large-scale Optimal Transport Problems
papers.contribution: For images at n=1024² pixels, achieves 8.9x speedup and 70.5% memory reduction; for 3D point clouds at scale 2^18, achieves 1.84x speedup and 83.2% memory reduction.

papers.title: Adaptive gradient descent on Riemannian manifolds and its applications to Gaussian variational inference
papers.contribution: Provides first convergence guarantee for Gaussian Variational Inference without L-smoothness assumption and demonstrates competitiveness in numerical simulations.

papers.title: An Efficient SE(p)-Invariant Transport Metric Driven by Polar Transport Discrepancy-based Representation
papers.contribution: Proves SEINT is well-defined metric with SE(p)-invariance, outperforms existing methods in classification and cross-space tasks, and enhances molecular generation as regularizer.

papers.title: Dimension-Free Multimodal Sampling via Preconditioned Annealed Langevin Dynamics
papers.contribution: Bridges gap between ALD empirical success and theory, establishing dimension-uniform stability under misspecified mixture score models via preconditioning.

papers.title: High-dimensional Mean-Field Games by Particle-based Flow Matching
papers.contribution: Proves convergence to stationary point sublinearly with linear convergence under convexity, demonstrates performance on non-potential MFGs and high-dimensional optimal transport problems.

papers.title: Random-projection ensemble dimension reduction
papers.contribution: Consistently matches or outperforms state-of-the-art methods across simulated and real datasets through flexible framework.

papers.title: Scalable Second-order Riemannian Optimization for $K$-means Clustering
papers.contribution: Converges significantly faster than state-of-the-art first-order methods while achieving similarly optimal statistical accuracy on cluster recovery.

papers.title: Variational inference via Gaussian interacting particles in the Bures-Wasserstein geometry
papers.contribution: Establishes well-posedness and convergence properties; demonstrates robustness and superior performance on variational inference tasks compared to gradient-based methods on non-log-concave targets.

papers.title: Achieving Structurally Robust Gromov Wasserstein Distance via Adaptive Dual-Mask
papers.contribution: The algorithm converges to a critical point under the Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz framework and achieves superior alignment quality on synthetic and real-world subgraph alignment benchmarks under severe structural noise.

papers.title: An Optimal Diffusion Approach to Quadratic Rate-Distortion Problems: New Solution and Approximation Methods
papers.contribution: Provides novel diffusion-based numerical method for estimating rate-distortion functions with demonstrated effectiveness on multiple examples.

papers.title: AvAtar: Learning to Align via Active Optimal Transport
papers.contribution: AvAtar demonstrates effectiveness, scalability, and generalizability on three representative alignment tasks including multimodal and point cloud registration.

papers.title: Complexity Analysis of Normalizing Constant Estimation: from Jarzynski Equality to Annealed Importance Sampling and beyond
papers.contribution: Derives oracle complexity bound of O-tilde(d*beta^2*A^2/epsilon^4) for estimating normalizing constants within relative error epsilon with high probability.

papers.title: Convex Distance Operator Transport: A Convex and Geometry-Preserving Formulation
papers.contribution: Achieves convexity while preserving geometry on attributed compact metric-measure spaces; derives non-asymptotic risk bounds and demonstrates better performance on point clouds, brain connectomes, and graph classification.

papers.title: Delving into Muon and Beyond: Deep Analysis and Extensions
papers.contribution: Reveals Muon as effective spectral normalization but not universally superior to Adam; RMS-normalized updates outperform first-moment updates for stable optimization.

papers.title: Elastic Optimal Transport: Theory, Application, and Empirical Evaluation
papers.contribution: ELOT significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on domain adaptation benchmarks while respecting data noise and outliers.

papers.title: Exploring Diverse Generation Paths via Inference-time Stiefel Activation Steering
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms standard sampling on test generation and discovery benchmarks with greater diversity without sacrificing performance.

papers.title: Fast Spectrally Sparse Signal Reconstruction via Jacobi-Preconditioned Gradient Descent
papers.contribution: Achieves linear convergence independent of condition number while maintaining low per-iteration complexity across broad problem settings.

papers.title: Geometric Convergence of Gauss–Newton for Neural Networks: Riemannian Geometry and Adaptive Damping
papers.contribution: Prove Gauss-Newton avoids kernel conditioning bottlenecks with geometric convergence rates independent of Gram-matrix conditioning.

papers.title: Gromov-Wasserstein at Scale, Beyond Squared Norms
papers.contribution: Scales to hundreds of thousands of points in minutes with strong theoretical guarantees; differentiable and enables exploration of GW energy landscape encoding matching symmetries.

papers.title: HOTA: Hamiltonian framework for Optimal Transport Advection
papers.contribution: Outperforms baselines on standard benchmarks and custom datasets with non-differentiable costs, in both feasibility and optimality.

papers.title: ITSPACE: Monotone Gaussian Optimal Transport Updates
papers.contribution: Achieves low-BW-gap solutions substantially faster than gradient-based methods and entropic regularization approaches on real-world covariance-alignment benchmarks.

papers.title: Incorporating Importance Weighting in Optimal Transport Based Domain Alignment
papers.contribution: The improved weighted bound converges to a nearest-neighbor alignment strategy and shows better performance than prior work across multiple distribution shifts.

papers.title: Inverse Entropic Optimal Transport Solves Semi-supervised Learning via Data Likelihood Maximization
papers.contribution: Demonstrates universal approximation property and effectively learns conditional distributions using combined data.

papers.title: Landing with the Score: Riemannian Optimization through Denoising
papers.contribution: Denoising Landing Flow and Denoising Riemannian Gradient Descent provide theoretical guarantees for manifold adherence and optimality on data-driven design problems.

papers.title: LoRA-S: An Efficient Low Rank Adaptation scheme via Sylvester equation
papers.contribution: Proposes AdamS and LRACS optimizers with runtime analysis, demonstrating improvements over existing LoRA optimizers.

papers.title: Muon in Associative Memory Learning: Training Dynamics and Scaling Laws
papers.contribution: Proves exponential speedup in noiseless case and derives scaling law for noisy power-law spectrum; validates through synthetic and LLaMA pretraining.

papers.title: Neural Hamilton--Jacobi Characteristic Flows for Optimal Transport
papers.contribution: Establishes a principled and versatile tool for optimal transport with provable optimality, demonstrating accuracy, scalability, and efficiency.

papers.title: Optimal Transport with Symmetry Groups
papers.contribution: First systematic incorporation of symmetry groups into optimal transport, providing theoretical framework and practical speedups on synthetic, real-world image, and molecular graph data.

papers.title: Rethinking the Flow-based Gradual Domain Adaptation: A Semi-Dual Optimal Transport Perspective
papers.contribution: Provides theoretical analysis of stability and generalization, with extensive experiments demonstrating the efficacy of the E-SUOT framework for constructing intermediate domains.

papers.title: Riemannian Dueling Optimization
papers.contribution: Extends dueling optimization to Riemannian manifolds with theoretical iteration and oracle complexity guarantees, validated on synthetic and real applications.

papers.title: Riemannian Neural Optimal Transport
papers.contribution: Approximates Riemannian OT maps with sub-exponential complexity in dimension and demonstrates improved scalability relative to discretization-based baselines.

papers.title: Riemannian Optimization on Relaxed Indicator Matrix Manifold
papers.contribution: RIM manifold optimization is O(n) versus O(n^3) for double stochastic methods and achieves better clustering results outperforming state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Riemannian Zeroth-Order Gradient Estimation with Structure-Preserving Metrics for Geodesically Incomplete Manifolds
papers.contribution: Establishes convergence guarantees for SGD matching best-known complexity in geodesically complete settings, with empirical validation on mesh optimization tasks.

papers.title: Riemannian stochastic optimization for sufficient dimension reduction
papers.contribution: Almost-sure convergence with non-asymptotic rate matching standard non-convex first-order scaling; matches or improves synthetic subspace recovery at high dimension and uniformly outperforms OPG with orders of magnitude lower runtime.

papers.title: Slicing Wasserstein over Wasserstein via Functional Optimal Transport
papers.contribution: DSW provides a computationally scalable and numerically stable alternative to Wasserstein-over-Wasserstein while maintaining equivalence for discretized meta-measures.

papers.title: SoftJAX & SoftTorch: Empowering Automatic Differentiation Libraries with Informative Gradients
papers.contribution: The libraries make soft relaxations easily accessible to differentiable programming, demonstrated through benchmarking and practical case studies.

papers.title: Spectra: Rethinking Optimizers for LLMs Under Spectral Anisotropy
papers.contribution: Across Qwen3 and LLaMA3 models, achieves lowest final validation loss and improves downstream accuracy by 1.41/0.89 and 1.62/0.66 points over AdamW/Muon; reaches matched loss targets up to 1.31× faster.

papers.title: Streaming Sliced Optimal Transport
papers.contribution: Stream-SW achieves more accurate approximation of SW than random subsampling with lower memory consumption on Gaussian and mixture distributions and diverse applications.

papers.title: Strongly Convex Sets in Riemannian Manifolds
papers.contribution: Shows that the Riemannian Frank-Wolfe algorithm converges linearly when Riemannian scaling inequalities hold.

papers.title: Variational Inference for Uncertain Optimal Transport via Sinkhorn Parametrization
papers.contribution: The method matches quality of intensive sampling techniques at a fraction of computational cost, scaling effectively to large-scale problems.

papers.title: You Need Better Attention Priors
papers.contribution: Provides an EOT-based explanation of attention sinks and learns an extrapolatable prior enabling better length generalization.
